seo_title: Delhi HC Fines Serial Litigant Rs 2 Lakh
title: Delhi HC Fines Serial Litigant Rs 2 Lakh, Bars Fresh Filings Until Costs Are Paid
case_name: Satya Prakash Ravidas v. SDM (HQ)/Registrar of Societies & Anr.
citation: W.P.(C) 16674/2026, order dated 6 November 2026, Amit Mahajan, J.
card_summary: The petitioner kept seeking an inquiry into a society, Raj Vidya Kender, and cancellation of its registration, after similar relief had already been refused. The Delhi High Court treated the fresh plea as an abuse of process, imposed Rs 2 lakh costs payable to its Legal Services Committee within four weeks, and barred the Registry from listing his further petitions until paid.
card_tip: Re-filing a plea a court has already refused does not just risk dismissal. A litigant who keeps doing it can be shut out of the Registry entirely until costs are paid, so check the earlier order before filing again.
verification_notes: Order number (W.P.(C) 16674/2026), date (6 November 2026), bench (Amit Mahajan, J.), the Rs 2 lakh costs figure, the four-week deadline to the Delhi High Court Legal Services Committee, and the bar on listing further petitions are consistent across LiveLaw (13 November 2026 report), Verdictum, which hosts a copy of the court's own order, and Court Book. The order's full text was not independently opened beyond the Verdictum-hosted copy and the press summaries, so the reasoning here is limited to what both sources state.
